limitations: Five stochastic samples per policy, not five independent datasets; no large-sample or cross-domain claim.
Inner cascades are proposal-utility proxies; root policy changes use native libRSI adoption and final audits use native tasks.
One child instruction per rewrite, then two formulas; five fixed samples are reused across native shadow and verification measurements.
Higher depths have more model work and token use per sample. Every actual call is counted; unchanged policies reuse identical final samples.
Same-depth default cascades are controls. Improvement from additional rewriting alone is not evidence that libRSI adopted a better root policy.
Official test set was used in earlier reports, but is absent from all model prompts and selection inputs in this run.
Native local timings include bookkeeping; inference is concurrent with up to three calls. Dollar billing and immutable model snapshot are unavailable.

Optimize out-of-sample MRR@5 using a reproducible anchor plus one controlled rarity experiment. The strongest supplied result was 0.66817 for idf*idf*(tf/(tf+0.6+0.4*length)+0.3*title_tf/(title_tf+1)); nearby idf*sqrt(idf) variants scored about 0.657–0.658. This is limited, confounded evidence, not proof of a universal optimum. Emit the strongest formula as proposal one unless it is active; if active, change its title coefficient to 0.25. For proposal two, preserve the strongest formula's frequency, length and title components, but replace idf*idf with idf*idf*sqrt(1+idf/4), testing moderately stronger rarity emphasis. Do not spend either slot on linear-IDF BM25, cosmetic rewrites or global rescaling. Return exactly two distinct, non-active formulas under the required schema, with reasons framed only as hypotheses. Check grammar, finite values and size limits. Use no tools or external evidence. If rewriting this strategy, preserve the anchor-and-controlled-experiment design.

Use the supplied feedback to propose a conservative strong anchor and a complementary term-coverage challenger, targeting reliable MRR@5 rather than tuning-score maximization. For the second formula retain idf*idf and the separate 0.3*title_tf/(title_tf+1) bonus, but replace the body component with tf/(tf+0.3+0.2*length). This controlled change saturates repeated mentions faster and reduces the length penalty, testing whether coverage of multiple distinctive query terms matters more than repetition. Do not infer independent validation sets from the five model samples or claim the IDF effect is isolated. Avoid extra interactions, linear-IDF fallbacks and arbitrary coefficient searches. Emit exactly two distinct non-active formulas, obeying all grammar, finiteness and size constraints; reasons must be hypotheses. No tools. Preserve this paired design through instruction rewrites.
